ownership_reason: Only the gold holds a property name together with the Properties object its value is read from; hops 1-4 hold the whole Properties object and the target ExtendedProperties and get back the filled target. The values a Properties object inherits from its default property lists can only be read through its getProperty (or listed through propertyNames); its defaults field is protected in java.util and no Commons Collections method flattens a Properties object, so no one-line change of a hop's arguments lets Hashtable.get see an inherited value, and once the gold has returned the target no caller can tell which inherited names were skipped. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the facade's javadoc ('this method will pick up any default parent Properties of the specified input object'); ExtendedProperties.getProperty does the same two-level lookup for the configuration class ('Will return user value if exists, if not then default value if exists'); ExtendedProperties.getString falls back to its defaults when a key has no value of its own; testCollections299 converts a Properties object with a default list and pins that only String values, own or inherited, are passed on; testRetrieve pins the target side (a value added with setProperty is returned by getProperty and getString, and an absent key gives null). The gold's javadoc promises the named properties of the Properties object with String values, and "resource.loader" is such a property (getProperty gives "class").
